messages:
Priya: Heads up — after the canary of Cilium 1.19.2 to west1-gpu at 10:12 UTC we're seeing intermittent packet loss for large-packet east-west flows between GPU pods (MTU 9000). Horovod jobs stall, and RDMA connections show reconnects. Canaries: gpu-n12..gpu-n15 affected.
infra-bot: Alert: retransmit spike detected in west1-gpu (10:15 UTC). aggregated_metric:net.retransmits > 3x baseline.
Alex: Which nodes exactly and any recent kernel or host changes? can you share a quick tcpdump or iperf result? :eyes:
Priya: Affected nodes listed above. Host kernel is 6.1.24 on those. Quick tcpdump from gpu-n12 (captured on the host veth):
```
13:23:45.123456 IP 10.240.5.12 > 10.240.5.14: UDP, len 65535
13:23:45.123457 IP 10.240.5.12 > 10.240.5.14: UDP, frag 1/2
13:23:45.123458 IP 10.240.5.12 > 10.240.5.14: UDP, frag 2/2
13:23:45.223999 IP 10.240.5.14 > 10.240.5.12: TCP 10.0.0.1:55234 > 10.0.0.2:22: Flags [R], seq 0, win 0
```
Packets look fragmented and not reassembled after the Cilium BPF program — retransmits and TCP resets show up on the app side.
Maria: I hit a similar issue on staging after enabling the new eBPF GSO path. iperf3 -M 65000 shows ~12-18% loss on large MSS. Commands I ran:
```
iperf3 -c <peer> -M 65000 -t 30
sudo ethtool -k eth0 | egrep "gso|gro|tso"
sysctl net.core.gso_max_size
```
Result: GSO enabled on host NIC, but kernel/GSO splitting seems not compatible with Cilium's new fragment handling.
Sam: Can we flip a config or rollback? Quick mitigation options: disable GSO acceleration in Cilium's datapath or revert to 1.18 for the cluster slice. If disabling, need cilium-agent restart on affected nodes.
Priya: Did a local test: set enable-gso: false in cilium-config on node gpu-n12 and restarted agent. Packet loss dropped from ~15% -> ~0-1% and Horovod job resumed. Workaround works.
Alex: Good. Please capture cilium-agent logs with debug level and include bpf map stats. Also check net.core.gso_max_size and any iproute2 fragmentation offloads.
Jay: Open an issue with Cilium upstream and include: kernel version, kubelet, cilium-agent log, tcpdump, iperf output, and node NIC offload settings. Also double-check tunnel MTU (we use GENEVE vxlan-like tunnel MTU 8950). MTU mismatch can exacerbate reassembly issues.
Priya: I'll file the ticket and attach artifacts. For immediate plan: pause further 1.19 rollout, roll back canary nodes to 1.18, and apply enable-gso: false as a hotfix clusterwide if needed.
infra-bot: Deploy bot: rollback job scheduled for 11:20 UTC. Change request: cilium -> 1.18.9 on west1-gpu canary nodes.
Maria: I created GH issue cilium/cilium#18642 and uploaded tcpdump + logs + the iperf output. Link: https://github.com/cilium/cilium/issues/18642
Sam: After rollback plan, let's run a controlled test with scaled iperf to confirm stable. Will coordinate a 30m window.
Alex: Also add kernel boot params and taint info in the bug report. There were kernel GSO fixes between 5.15 and 6.x that interact with BPF sometimes.
Priya: Thanks all — I'll post updates here after rollback and when Cilium responds. For now canary pause in place. :thumbsup:
